Cathay General Bancorp Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results

 

Los Angeles, Calif., October 21, 2026: Cathay General Bancorp (the “Company”, “we”, “us”, or “our”) (Nasdaq: CATY), the holding company for Cathay Bank, today announced its unaudited financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. The Company reported net income of $95.2 million, or $1.43 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2026 compared to $92.2 million, or $1.37 per diluted share for the second quarter of 2026.

 

“Our third quarter results reflected strong performance across the franchise. Net interest income grew, loans and deposits increased meaningfully, and net interest margin continued to expand,” said Chang M. Liu, President and Chief Executive Officer of the Company. “We remain focused on disciplined execution and prudent balance sheet management to build on this progress and continue delivering long-term value for our shareholders.”

●

Record net interest income of $211.9 million, an increase of $11.0 million, or 5.5%, from the second quarter of 2026.

 

●

Net interest margin expanded four basis points to 3.52% from 3.48% in the second quarter of 2026.

 

●

Total loans, excluding loans held for sale, increased $574.5 million, or 2.79% sequentially to $21.20 billion, representing approximately 11.4% annualized growth.

 

●

Total deposits increased $773.3 million, or 3.67%, sequentially to $21.83 billion, supporting strong loan growth and strategic balance sheet positioning.

 

●

Nonperforming assets declined $26.2 million, or 18.0%, and the ratio of nonperforming assets to total assets improved to 0.47% from 0.59%.

 

●

The provision for credit losses was $28.6 million, primarily reflecting strong loan growth and updated loss assumptions incorporating recent charge-off experience.

 

●

The Company completed the redemption of $54.1 million of Trust Preferred Securities (“TruPS”), representing approximately 45% of the Company's $119.1 million of outstanding TruPS.

 

INCOME STATEMENT REVIEW

THIRD QUARTER 2026 COMPARED TO THE SECOND QUARTER 2026

 

Net income for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, was $95.2 million, an increase of $3.0 million, or 3.3%, compared to net income of $92.2 million for the second quarter of 2026. Diluted earnings per share for the third quarter of 2026 was $1.43 per share compared to $1.37 per share for the second quarter of 2026.

 

Return on average stockholders’ equity was 12.28% and return on average assets was 1.51% for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to a return on average stockholders’ equity of 12.21% and a return on average assets of 1.52% in the second quarter of 2026.

 

Net interest income before provision for credit losses

 

Net interest income before provision for credit losses increased $11.0 million, or 5.5%, to $211.9 million during the third quarter of 2026, compared to $200.9 million in the second quarter of 2026. The increase was due primarily to an increase in interest income from loans and deposits with banks and partially offset by an increase in deposit interest expense.

 

The net interest margin was 3.52% for the third quarter of 2026 compared to 3.48% for the second quarter of 2026.

 

For the third quarter of 2026, the yield on average interest-earning assets was 5.74%, the cost of funds on average interest-bearing liabilities was 2.93%, and the cost of average interest-bearing deposits was 2.91%. In comparison, for the second quarter of 2026, the yield on average interest-earning assets was 5.66%, the cost of funds on average interest-bearing liabilities was 2.89%, and the cost of average interest-bearing deposits was 2.86%. The increase in the cost of funds on average interest-bearing liabilities resulted mainly from higher interest rates on deposits, driven by the higher repricing of maturing time deposits in the third quarter. The increase in the yield on average interest-earning assets resulted mainly from higher interest rates on loans. The net interest spread, defined as the difference between the yield on average interest-earning assets and the cost of funds on average interest-bearing liabilities, was 2.81% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 2.77% for the second quarter of 2026.

 

Provision for credit losses

 

The Company recorded a provision for credit losses of $28.6 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to $11.2 million in the second quarter of 2026. The higher provision primarily reflected strong loan growth and updated loss assumptions incorporating recent charge-off experience. Nonperforming assets declined $26.2 million, or 18.0%, during the quarter, and the ratio of nonperforming assets to total assets improved to 0.47% from 0.59%. As of September 30, 2026, the allowance for loan losses increased by $5.3 million to $224.2 million, or 1.06% of gross loans, compared to $218.9 million, or 1.06% of gross loans as of June 30, 2026.

 

Net charge-offs of $25.3 million, or 0.48% of average loans on an annualized basis, were concentrated in three borrower-specific credits, including one construction loan and two movie theater CRE loans acquired from Far East National Bank.

Non-interest income

 

Non-interest income, which includes revenues from depository service fees, letters of credit commissions, securities gains (losses), wealth management fees, and other sources of fee income, was $42.8 million for the third quarter of 2026, an increase of $21.4 million, or 99.8%, compared to $21.4 million for the second quarter of 2026. The increase was primarily driven by a $24.4 million increase in net gains from equity securities and a $3.1 million benefit from the redemption of TruPS, partially offset by a $4.5 million increase in losses related to investment securities repositioning activities and a $1.3 million decrease in wealth management fees.

 

Non-interest expense

 

Non-interest expense increased $11.1 million, or 12.0%, to $103.4 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to $92.3 million in the second quarter of 2026. The increase was primarily attributable to an $8.0 million charitable contribution to the Cathay Bank Foundation, a $5.4 million contract termination fee, and a $1.5 million increase in salaries and employee benefits, partially offset by a $3.4 million decrease in the amortization of investments in low-income housing and alternative energy partnerships. The efficiency ratio, defined as non-interest expense divided by the sum of net interest income before provision for credit losses plus non-interest income, was 40.60% in the third quarter of 2026 compared to 41.53% for the second quarter of 2026.

 

Income taxes

 

The effective tax rate for the third quarter of 2026 was 22.42% compared to 22.35% for the second quarter of 2026, primarily due to the higher pre-tax income in the third quarter of 2026. The effective tax rate for the third quarter of 2026 and second quarter of 2026 includes the impact of low-income housing tax credits.

 

BALANCE SHEET REVIEW

 

Gross loans, excluding loans held for sale, increased $574.5 million, or 2.79%, to $21.20 billion as of September 30, 2026, from $20.62 billion as of June 30, 2026. The increase was primarily due to increases of $420.4 million, or 11.9%, in commercial loans; $73.3 million, or 1.3%, in residential real estate loans; $65.5 million, or 0.6%, in commercial real estate loans; and $17.5 million, or 7.0%, in construction loans, partially offset by a decrease of $6.4 million, or 2.7%, in equity lines.

ASSET QUALITY REVIEW

 

As of September 30, 2026, total non-accrual loans were $87.3 million, a decrease of $24.4 million, or 21.8%, from $111.7 million as of June 30, 2026.

 

The allowance for loan losses was $224.2 million and the allowance for off-balance sheet unfunded credit commitments was $12.9 million as of September 30, 2026. Together, these allowances represent the amount estimated by management to be appropriate to absorb expected credit losses inherent in the loan portfolio, including unfunded credit commitments. The allowance for loan losses represented 1.06% of period-end gross loans, and 242.97% of non-performing loans as of September 30, 2026. The comparable ratios were 1.06% of period-end gross loans, and 195.97% of non-performing loans as of June 30, 2026.

The ratio of non-performing assets to total assets decreased to 0.47% as of September 30, 2026, from 0.59% as of June 30, 2026. Total non-performing assets decreased $26.2 million, or 18.0%, to $119.2 million as of September 30, 2026, from $145.4 million as of June 30, 2026. The decrease was primarily due to decreases of $24.4 million, or 21.8%, in non-accrual loans and $6.7 million, or 20.1%, in other real estate owned, partially offset by an increase of $5.0 million, or 100.0%, in accruing loans past due 90 days or more.

 

CAPITAL ADEQUACY REVIEW

 

As of September 30, 2026, the Company’s Common Equity Tier 1 risk-based capital ratio of 13.51%, Tier 1 risk-based capital ratio of 13.51%,total risk-based capital ratio of 15.00%, and Tier 1 leverage capital ratio of 11.06%, calculated under the Basel III capital rules, exceeded applicable minimum regulatory capital requirements, including the fully phased-in 2.5% capital conservation buffer applicable to the risk-based capital ratios. As of June 30, 2026, the Company’s Common Equity Tier 1 risk-based capital ratio was 13.70%, Tier 1 risk-based capital ratio was 13.70%,total risk-based capital ratio was 15.47%, and Tier 1 leverage capital ratio was 11.28%.

 

YEAR-TO-DATE REVIEW

 

Net income for the nine months ending September 30, 2026, was $274.3 million, an increase of $49.7 million, or 22.1%, compared to net income of $224.6 million for the same period a year ago. Diluted earnings per share for the nine months ending September 30, 2026 was $4.09 per share compared to $3.21 per share for the same period a year ago. The net interest margin for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was 3.48% compared to 3.28% for the same period a year ago.

 

Return on average stockholders’ equity was 12.13% and return on average assets was 1.50% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to a return on average stockholders’ equity of 10.39% and a return on average assets of 1.28% for the same period a year ago. The efficiency ratio for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was 40.82% compared to 44.18% for the same period a year ago.

ABOUT CATHAY GENERAL BANCORP

 

Cathay General Bancorp is a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: CATY) and is the holding company for Cathay Bank, a California state-chartered bank.  Founded in 1962, Cathay Bank offers a wide range of financial services and currently operates over 60 branches across the United States in California, New York, Washington, Texas, Illinois, Massachusetts, Maryland, Nevada, and New Jersey. Overseas, it has a branch outlet in Hong Kong, and representative offices in Beijing, Shanghai, Taipei and Ho Chi Minh City. To learn more about Cathay Bank, please visit www.cathaybank.com. Cathay General Bancorp’s website is at www.cathaygeneralbancorp.com. Information set forth on such websites is not incorporated into this press release.

CATHAY GENERAL BANCORP

GAAP to NON-GAAP RECONCILIATION

SELECTED CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL INFORMATION

(Unaudited)

 

The Company uses certain non-GAAP financial measures including tangible book value (“TBV”), tangible book value per share (“TBV/Share”), tangible assets, tangible common equity (“TCE”) ratio, the return on average tangible common stockholders’ equity (“ROATCE”), adjusted total revenue, adjusted non-interest expense, and the adjusted efficiency ratio. We believe these non-GAAP financial measures provide investors with information useful in understanding its financial position, results of operations, the strength of its capital position, and overall business performance. These non-GAAP financial measures are used for performance measurement purposes, as well as for internal planning and forecasting, and by securities analysts, investors, and other interested parties to assess peer company operating performance. These non-GAAP financial measures should not be considered a substitute for GAAP-basis financial measures. Because non-GAAP financial measures are not standardized, it may not be possible to compare these with other companies that present financial measures having the same or similar names. The Company strongly encourages investors to review its consolidated financial statements in their entirety and to not rely on any single financial measure.

 

TBV represents stockholders’ equity less goodwill and other intangible assets. TBV/share represents TBV divided by the number of common shares outstanding at the end of the reporting period. The TCE ratio represents TBV divided by tangible assets. Tangible assets is equal to total assets less goodwill and other intangible assets. ROATCE is calculated using net income adjusted for the tax-effected amortization of intangible assets, as a percentage of average stockholders’ equity less average goodwill and other intangible assets.

- 14 -

 

Adjusted total revenue is calculated by adding net interest income before provision for credit losses and non-interest income excluding net gains and losses from equity and investment securities and TruPS redemption benefit. Adjusted non-interest expense is non-interest expense excluding amortization of investments in low-income housing and alternative energy partnerships, other real estate owned expenses, amortization of core deposit intangibles, the FDIC special assessment, charitable contribution to Cathay Bank Foundation and contract termination costs. The Adjusted efficiency ratio is calculated by dividing the Company’s adjusted non‑interest expense by adjusted total revenue. It represents the costs expended to generate a dollar of revenue. The adjusted components exclude items that are non‑operational as well as the amortization of investments in low‑income housing partnerships and alternative energy partnerships. Although this amortization is operational in nature, it is removed to enhance comparability with peers that report these costs within income tax expense under proportional amortization accounting, which the Company has not yet adopted.
